note: Protocol validation run (NOT a score run): can a frame-sequence evaluator distinguish real temporal phenomena from VLM 'looks like' judgments? 4 motion atoms x 2 model families x 2 scenes x 2 conditions = 32 clips, 5s each. Red line per docs/BENCHMARK.md 4.2: video terms must be judged on CONTINUOUS FRAMES, never a single mid-frame. dolly zoom requires BOTH subject-scale stability AND background perspective change.

scenes.prompt: a street scene with a cyclist passing by
a woman walking through a park

questions.tracking shot: These 6 frames are sampled in order from one 5-second video (control: no camera term / treatment: with 'tracking shot'). Based on the FRAME SEQUENCE, does the camera clearly track the moving subject — i.e., subject apparent size stays roughly stable while the background shifts consistently with camera following? A static camera with a moving subject = NO. Answer YES or NO only.
questions.handheld: These 6 frames are sampled in order from one 5-second video (control / treatment: with 'handheld'). Based on the FRAME SEQUENCE, does the footage show non-regular, non-mechanical handheld-style camera micro-jitter — framing shifts unevenly between frames (horizon tilt/offset varies irregularly)? Smooth gimbal/steadicam or perfectly static framing = NO. Answer YES or NO only.
questions.dolly zoom: These 6 frames are sampled in order from one 5-second video (control / treatment: with 'dolly zoom'). Based on the FRAME SEQUENCE, does the video show a dolly zoom (vertigo effect): the main subject's apparent size stays roughly STABLE while the background perspective/field-of-view clearly CHANGES (background appears to warp/stretch)? BOTH conditions required — subject stable AND background perspective changing. Either one alone = NO. Answer YES or NO only.
questions.long take: These 6 frames are sampled in order from one 5-second video (control / treatment: with 'long take'). Based on the FRAME SEQUENCE, is this a continuous single take — no shot boundary, no sudden scene/discontinuity jump between consecutive frames? Any clear cut = NO. Answer YES or NO only.
